extra.message: Broken Object Level Authorization in get_by_username — Unauthorized access to any user's details (username, email, admin status, and likely password). [verified: get_by_username (lines 45-46) lacks any authentication or authorization check; it directly calls User.get_user(username) and returns the string representation of the user object, exposing all fields including password. No compensating control such as token validation is present.]

Mass Assignment Privilege Escalation in register_user — Attacker can register as an administrator, gaining full control over the application. [verified: The code at lines 60-66 directly accepts an 'admin' property from the request body when the `vuln` flag is true, and there is no schema restriction (default JSON Schema allows additional properties) or other control to prevent this. An attacker can register as an admin without authentication.]

Debug Mode Enabled — Remote code execution via Werkzeug debugger, leading to full server compromise. [verified: The Flask application runs with debug=True and is bound to 0.0.0.0, making the Werkzeug debugger remotely accessible. No authentication or compensating controls prevent an attacker from reaching the debugger console or triggering errors to leverage arbitrary code execution.]

Password Exposure via Debug Endpoint — An attacker can retrieve all users' passwords, leading to unauthorized access to all accounts including admin. [verified: The /debug endpoint calls get_all_users_debug() which returns json_debug including plain-text passwords; no authentication or authorization is enforced on this endpoint.]

SQL Injection in get_user — An attacker can extract arbitrary data from the database, including passwords, modify or delete data, and potentially achieve remote code execution in some configurations. [verified: The get_user method at line 72 directly concatenates the username parameter into an SQL query string when the 'vuln' flag is True, without any sanitization or parameterization. The username originates from the URL path of the /users/{username} endpoint and is not validated, making SQL injection possible.]

Missing Authorization for get_all_books — Unauthenticated disclosure of all book data, including secret content. [verified: Function get_all_books() at line 13 returns Book.get_all_books() without any authentication or authorization check, allowing unauthenticated access to all book data including secret_content.]

Broken Object Level Authorization in get_by_title — Authenticated user can read any book's secret content, regardless of ownership. [verified: When vuln flag is True (line 50), get_by_title() queries Book by title without filtering by user (line 51), allowing any authenticated user to read any book's secret content regardless of ownership. No compensating authorization control exists.]

Missing Authorization for get_all_users — Complete exposure of all user PII, including passwords, to any unauthenticated attacker. [verified: The get_all_users function on line 19-21 returns User.get_all_users() without any authentication or authorization check, allowing any unauthenticated attacker to access all user records including passwords stored in plaintext.]

Missing Authorization in User Lookup — An attacker can enumerate usernames and access PII (email) of any user, violating privacy. [verified: The get_user function at models/user_model.py:70 retrieves user data by username without any authorization check; it is called from the GET /users/{username} endpoint which accepts attacker-controlled input, and no compensating control prevents an authenticated user from querying any user's email.]

Password Enumeration via Error Messages in login_user — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames, facilitating targeted password guessing attacks. [verified: When vuln is True (line 101), the login endpoint returns distinct error messages for existing vs. non-existing users (lines 102-106), enabling username enumeration. No compensating controls (rate limiting, generic messaging) exist in this path.]
